title: Keyed token-bucket limiter: exhausted buckets are falsy and replaced; sweep reads stale token counts

hidden_checks.spec: Symptom 1 reproduction: expected [True]*5 + [False]*3.
Rules 2/3: the key's bucket is kept and reused regardless of tokens; retry_after/remaining semantics.
Rule 2: bucket kept and reused for every later request regardless of how many tokens it holds; rule 1 continuous refill.
Rules 1/2: a bucket starts full, holds at most capacity, and is reused (no fresh buckets).
Rules 1/3: try_take takes cost tokens only if available; retry_after = ceil(wait_time(cost)); remaining = len(bucket).
Rule 2: each key has its own bucket; rule 4 len(limiter) reflects stored buckets.
Rule 3: when rejected retry_after is ceil(wait_time(cost)) whole seconds and at least 1.
Rule 3: a request made exactly retry_after seconds after a rejection is allowed.
Rule 1: ValueError unless 0 < cost <= capacity.
Rule 1: len(bucket) is the number of whole tokens available now (floor) and must keep working.
Rule 1: is_full() is True iff the bucket, refilled up to the current clock time, holds capacity tokens.
Rule 1: if the clock goes backwards no time passes and the reference time never moves backwards.
Rule 1: try_take returns False and takes nothing; wait_time is 0.0 if available now.
Symptom 2 reproduction: expected sweep() == 2 and len(lim) == 0.
Rule 4: removes buckets idle >= idle_ttl that are full at the current time; a returning key gets a new full bucket.
Rule 4: only buckets with idle_for() >= idle_ttl are removed.
Rule 4: a bucket that is not full at the current time is kept.
Rule 1: idle_for() counts from the last try_take, allowed or not; rule 4 boundary >=.
Rule 4: removes every qualifying bucket and returns how many; key in limiter reflects stored buckets.
Rule 5: policy.parse keeps its current behavior (units, (count, count/seconds), ValueError otherwise).
Rule 5: KeyedLimiter.from_policy; rules 2/3 enforcement.
